# How much of our electric bill is one bad 15 minutes, and what would it take to remove it?

> Free tool for businesses with demand charges: paste 15-minute utility interval data or open the Green Button CSV or XML file as downloaded (XML converted to local clock time with daylight saving) and see monthly peaks, demand charges, ratchet effects, and what shaving the peak would save and need. With time-of-use rates it plans one battery month by month, minimising demand and energy charges together with an exact linear programme solved in the browser (peak shaving plus arbitrage: charge off-peak, discharge on-peak), and splits the saving into demand and energy. With a demand ratchet, when an earlier peak's floor sets a month's bill it also plans the whole period as one programme with the ratchet inside it, so the battery is not spent on peaks the floor already bills. Paste your utility's actual rate from OpenEI's Utility Rate Database (URDB JSON) and the bill is priced with its seasons, every demand period, the seasonal all-hours demand charge, riders, the demand window and optional holidays, and the battery is planned against all of them at once (checked against HiGHS on 288 building-months under two real rates: within 29 cents a month). Nothing uploaded.

Free and open source (MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.
